# Renofy — Full content map for AI systems

> This is the extended companion to https://renofy.ca/llms.txt. It summarizes every public page of renofy.ca in plain markdown so AI assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot) can answer questions about Renofy accurately and cite the right page.

## Company overview

Renofy is a full-home renovation company based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, serving Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area (GTA). Kitchen and bathroom renovations are its flagship specialties; it also renovates basements, installs flooring, paints interiors, does drywall/plaster work, and fabricates quartz, quartzite, and natural stone countertops — including full-height stone backsplashes and waterfall islands. Renofy does NOT install tile backsplashes (deliberate policy; floor tile in porcelain/ceramic is offered for floors).

Business model: fixed written quotes signed before work starts (price only changes if the client changes scope), milestone-based payments (never full payment upfront), permits and inspections handled in-house, dust-controlled job sites (sealed work zones, negative-air scrubbers, daily cleanup), and a 1-year craftsmanship warranty.

Key numbers: 7 years of experience, 250+ completed projects, rated 4.9/5. Free consultations and free instant estimates with no email required.

### Kitchen renovation cost in Toronto (2026 guide) — https://renofy.ca/kitchen-renovation-cost-toronto.html
2026 GTA price ranges: cosmetic refresh (paint, hardware, counters, no layout change) $25,000–$40,000, 2–3 weeks; mid-range full renovation $45,000–$75,000, 5–7 weeks; high-end / layout change $75,000–$100,000, 6–8 weeks; luxury custom (custom millwork, full-height stone, professional appliances) $100,000+, 8–12 weeks. Biggest cost drivers: layout changes and moving plumbing/gas, custom cabinetry/millwork, stone selection, appliance tier. Typical full kitchen: $45,000–$90,000.

### Bathroom renovation cost in Toronto (2026 guide) — https://renofy.ca/bathroom-renovation-cost-toronto.html
2026 GTA price ranges: powder room refresh $15,000–$25,000, 2–3 weeks; full bathroom renovation $28,000–$60,000, 3–5 weeks; luxury primary ensuite (curbless shower, heated floors) $60,000–$90,000, 5–7 weeks. Single biggest cost adder: moving plumbing (relocating toilet or shower drain means opening floors and re-routing stacks).

### FAQ — https://renofy.ca/faq.html
12 questions with direct answers:
1. How much does a kitchen renovation cost in Toronto? — $45,000–$90,000 typical; luxury $100,000+; cosmetic refresh $25,000–$40,000. Layout changes are the biggest cost driver.
2. How much does a bathroom renovation cost in Toronto? — $28,000–$60,000 typical; luxury ensuites $70,000+. Moving plumbing is the biggest cost adder.
3. How long does a renovation take? — Bathrooms 3–5 weeks, kitchens 5–8 weeks, basements 6–10 weeks. Written schedule provided before day one.
4. Are your quotes really fixed? — Yes: detailed, in writing, signed before starting. Price changes only if the client changes scope.
5. Do you handle permits and inspections? — Yes, permits coordinated and inspections signed off; clients never deal with the city.
6. Will my home be livable during the renovation? — Almost always yes: sealed work zones, negative-air scrubbers, daily cleaning; full-home projects are phased so a working kitchen remains.
7. Do you install tile backsplashes? — No. Countertops and backsplashes are quartz, quartzite, or natural stone only (full-height stone backsplashes, waterfall islands); no grout lines to re-seal.
8. What areas do you serve? — Toronto and the GTA: 10 regions / 21 cities (see Service areas below).
9. Is the consultation really free? — Yes: free consult and free instant website estimate, no email required, no pressure.
10. What warranty do you offer? — 1-year craftsmanship warranty; warranty work is done free.
11. Do I need to move out during the renovation? — Not for single-room projects; full-home projects can be phased so clients may stay.
12. How do payments work? — Milestone-based (deposit, rough-in, finishes, final walkthrough); never full payment upfront.
